L01-AN.title: Find flights with AN
L01-AN.objective: Request an availability display for a travel date and a city pair, and read the flight lines.
L01-AN.body:
Amadeus is a reservation system that travel agencies and airlines use to look up flights, build bookings, and price trips. In the workplace, when a passenger asks to travel, a reservation agent types short text commands (entries) into Amadeus to create the passenger's booking record, called a PNR. In DEIXEN, you practise the reservation agent's role in a training simulator using fictional flights and fares. Across nine required steps, you will search for flights (AN), sell a seat (SS), add the passenger's name (NM), add the agency phone (AP), pass the passenger's mobile contact or refusal to the airline (SRCTCM or SRCTCR), set the ticketing arrangement (TK), record who requested the booking (RF), end the transaction to save the booking (ER), and price it (FXP). Step ten (FQD) is an optional fare display.

Your first step as the reservation agent is to check which flights are available for the passenger's trip. The command AN requests an availability display: a list of flights between two cities that have at least one seat available to book. In the entry, the origin (departure city) and the destination (arrival city) are each written as a short code, such as RUH for Riyadh, and the two codes written together form a city pair. Build the entry in three parts with no spaces: the fixed command code AN, the travel date as a two-digit day and three-letter English month (such as 15OCT or 14FEB), and the six-letter city pair. You may also add a four-digit departure time in 24-hour format at the end. For example, in DEIXEN's demonstration booking for Riyadh (RUH) to Jeddah (JED) on 15 October, the entry is AN15OCTRUHJED; with a departure time in the official Amadeus example for Stockholm (STO) to Frankfurt (FRA) on 14 February at 17:00, the entry is AN14FEBSTOFRA1700.

In DEIXEN's demonstration booking, entering AN15OCTRUHJED returns an availability display like this: the header line ** AN JEDDAH.SA                  15OCT26 0000  (30)TH 15OCT 0000, followed by flight lines such as 1   6X 101  J9 C9 Y9 B9 M9  RUH   JED    0700 0840  E0/320      1:40. On the header line, AN is the display name, JEDDAH.SA is the destination name and country code, TH is the two-letter weekday, 15OCT is the date, and 0000 is the time. On each flight line, read from left to right: the line number (1), the two-character airline code and flight number (6X 101), the booking classes offered as single letters (J, C, Y, B, M), the origin and destination codes (RUH and JED), the departure time (0700) and arrival time (0840), the three-character equipment code after the slash (320, identifying the aircraft type), and the flying time at the end (1:40). Three details on this display are not taught in DEIXEN because their exact meaning is not verified in official Amadeus sources: the number in parentheses before the weekday ((30)), the figure after each booking class letter (such as 9 in Y9), and the E0 code before the slash. In the demonstration and Terminal views, you can press Show names to see every labelled part of the display.

In Amadeus, an availability display covers dates from 3 days in the past up to 361 days in the future. Flights are listed in three groups: non-stop flights first (direct from origin to destination with no stop), then direct flights (flights that make an intermediate stop using the same flight number and aircraft), and finally connecting flights (trips that change flight number or aircraft at a connecting city). If a reservation agent wants an availability display for one specific airline only, the two-character airline code is placed immediately after AN before the date, as in the official example ANMH06NOVKULSIN (for airline MH on 06NOV from KUL to SIN). Your DEIXEN task uses a general availability entry without an airline code after AN.

Keep two values from the flight line that matches your task brief: the line number and the booking class letter, because the next step (SS) uses both.
L02-SS.title: Sell a seat with SS
L02-SS.objective: Reserve seats in a booking class from a line of the availability display using SS, and read the sold flight line in the booking.
L02-SS.body:
Once the availability display is open, the reservation agent reserves seats on the chosen flight. In Amadeus, reserving a seat is called selling a seat, and selling directly by referring to a line number on an open availability display is called a short sell. Look back at the availability display from step 1 and recall the two values you identified on the flight line that matches the passenger's trip: the booking class letter requested in the task and the line number at the far left of that flight.

Build the short-sell entry in four parts with no spaces: the fixed command code SS, the number of seats to reserve, the single-letter booking class, and the line number from the availability display. In DEIXEN's practice tasks, the number of seats always equals the number of passengers in the task brief. For example, to reserve 1 seat in booking class M from line 3 of an availability display, type SS1M3 (or in DEIXEN's demonstration booking, SS1M1 for 1 seat in booking class M on line 1).

When the system accepts SS, it adds the flight to the PNR and displays the booking as it now stands. In DEIXEN's demonstration booking after SS1M1, the response shows a header line RP/XXXXXXXXX/ and the sold flight line: 1  6X 101 M 15OCT 4 RUHJED HK1       0700 0840   320 E 0. On the header line, RP/ marks the start of the booking header and XXXXXXXXX represents the hidden office ID (the identification code of the booking office). On the sold flight line, read from left to right: the element number (1, showing this item's current position in the booking), the airline code and flight number (6X 101), the booking class letter (M), the travel date (15OCT), the day of the week as a single digit (4), the origin and destination codes written together (RUHJED), the status code and seat count (HK1, where HK means the reservation is confirmed and 1 is the number of seats confirmed), the departure time (0700) and arrival time (0840), and the equipment code (320). The single-letter codes after the equipment code (such as E 0 here, or M R in the official Amadeus example) are not taught in DEIXEN because official Amadeus sources do not state their meaning. You can now move to the next step to add the passenger's name with NM.
L03-NM.title: Add the passenger name with NM
L03-NM.objective: Enter the passenger's name element with NM using the passenger count, surname, first name, and title, and read the renumbered booking display.
L03-NM.body:
After reserving the flight, the reservation agent records who is travelling by adding a name element to the PNR. In Amadeus, every PNR must contain five mandatory elements before it can be saved, remembered by the word PRINT: Phone (a contact telephone number), Received from (who requested the booking), Itinerary (at least one booked flight), Name (the passenger's name), and Ticketing (the ticketing arrangement). Step 2 added the itinerary; this step adds the Name element with the command NM.

Build the name entry in five parts: the fixed command code NM, a single digit for the number of passengers sharing the same surname (with no space after NM), the passenger's surname (family name), a slash (/), the passenger's first name (given name), a single space, and the title (such as MR or MRS). In this DEIXEN slice, you practise booking one adult passenger at a time, so the count after NM is 1. For example, in the pattern from official Amadeus documentation for one passenger named Tom Jones with title MR, the entry is NM1JONES/TOM MR (and in DEIXEN's demonstration booking for Mr Omar Salem, it is NM1SALEM/OMAR MR). Make sure the surname comes before the slash, the first name comes after the slash, and a single space separates the first name from the title.

When Amadeus adds the name element, it places passenger names at the top of the PNR before the flight lines. In DEIXEN's demonstration booking after NM1SALEM/OMAR MR, the booking display under RP/XXXXXXXXX/ reads: element 1 is 1.SALEM/OMAR MR, and element 2 is 2  6X 101 M 15OCT 4 RUHJED HK1       0700 0840   320 E 0. On element 1, 1 is the element number, SALEM is the surname, OMAR is the first name, and MR is the title. Notice that the flight you sold in step 2 has moved from element 1 to element 2: in a booking display, element numbers always show each item's current line position in the PNR. Next, you will add the agency phone number to the booking with AP.
L04-AP.title: Add a contact with AP
L04-AP.objective: Add the booking's phone contact element with AP using the telephone number given in the task, and recognize the stored AP element.
L04-AP.body:
A booking record can carry a contact element. The reservation agent adds a contact element with the command AP. In this DEIXEN training task, the agency phone number is added using AP. In Amadeus, the text after AP is free text, meaning the system accepts telephone numbers and contact words without requiring a fixed internal punctuation pattern. In DEIXEN's tasks, you enter the agency telephone number given in your task brief.

Build the entry in two parts: the fixed command code AP, followed immediately by the contact telephone number as free text. For example, in DEIXEN's demonstration booking with the fictional agency telephone number 966120000000, the entry is AP966120000000 (and an official Amadeus example with a city and extension suffix is AP94670606-B). In your DEIXEN task, write AP followed directly by the agency phone number from your brief.

In the booking display, the stored contact appears as its own numbered element after the flight line. In DEIXEN's demonstration booking after AP966120000000, element 3 reads: 3 AP 966120000000, where 3 is the element number, AP identifies the contact element, and 966120000000 is the contact text. Because official Amadeus sources verify the stored AP element inside a completed PNR (V-18) rather than a separate immediate response screen after typing AP alone, DEIXEN displays the updated booking with a dashed line and a note reminding you not to memorise small unverified screen details. Note that the AP contact element is separate from the airline operational contact you will add in the next step (SRCTCM or SRCTCR).
L05-CTC.title: Pass the passenger's contact to the airline: SRCTCM (and SRCTCR)
L05-CTC.objective: Transfer the passenger's mobile number to the airline with SRCTCM, or record the passenger's refusal with SRCTCR, and recognize the stored contact SSR element.
L05-CTC.body:
In addition to the booking's AP phone element, international airline rules under IATA Resolution 830d require reservation agents to ask the passenger for a mobile telephone number or e-mail address and pass it to the airline — or record that the passenger declined to share it. Airlines use this contact during irregular operations, such as flight delays, cancellations, or schedule changes. In Amadeus, this information is stored as a Special Service Request (SSR): a structured message element sent to the airline inside the PNR, separate from the AP element.

Choose the entry that matches what the passenger tells you in the task brief. When the passenger gives a mobile number for the airline, use SRCTCM: write the fixed command code SRCTCM, a mandatory dash (-), and the digits of the passenger's mobile number with no spaces or punctuation. For example, in DEIXEN's demonstration booking with the fictional mobile number 966500000009, the entry is SRCTCM-966500000009. When the passenger refuses to share a mobile number or e-mail address, never invent a number; instead, record the refusal with SRCTCR by writing the fixed command code SRCTCR, a mandatory dash (-), and short free text stating the refusal, such as SRCTCR-REFUSED.

When you enter SRCTCM-966500000009 in DEIXEN's demonstration booking, the stored element appears in the booking display as: 4 SSR CTCM 6X HK1 966500000009. Here, 4 is the element number, SSR CTCM identifies the mobile-contact Special Service Request, and 966500000009 is the passenger's mobile number; the airline code (6X) and HK1 inside this stored line are not taught in DEIXEN because official Amadeus sources do not explain their role on a stored CTCM line. When you enter SRCTCR-REFUSED (as in the Scenario task), DEIXEN records the refusal with a training message — Contact refusal recorded (SRCTCR): REFUSED. — because no official Amadeus example shows the exact screen format of a stored SRCTCR line.

Official Amadeus examples also show endings after a slash, such as SRCTCM-3054996244/US and SRCTCR-REFUSED/P3; what follows that slash is outside this slice, and DEIXEN accepts your entry without it. Amadeus also has an e-mail contact command (SRCTCE, not simulated in this slice). If a booking has none of SRCTCM, SRCTCE, or SRCTCR when the reservation agent tries to end the transaction with ER, Amadeus displays a warning.
L06-TK.title: Set the ticketing arrangement with TK
L06-TK.objective: Add the ticketing arrangement element with TK that matches the task brief, and read the stored TK element in the booking.
L06-TK.body:
Creating a PNR reserves the passenger's seat, and issuing the ticket is a separate step. Every PNR needs a ticketing arrangement element — the T in PRINT — to state how or when the ticket is to be issued. The reservation agent adds this element with the command TK.

Amadeus provides two ticketing arrangement entries here. When the task specifies that the booking is ready for immediate ticketing (or gives TKOK), enter the four-letter command TKOK with no spaces. When a time limit is needed for ticketing on a specific date, enter TKTL followed immediately by the two-digit day and three-letter English month, as in the official Amadeus example TKTL10OCT. In DEIXEN's main task and scenario, the task brief specifies TKOK.

When you enter TKOK in DEIXEN's demonstration booking, the stored element appears in the booking display before the SSR elements: 4 TK OK25SEP/XXXXXXXXX (while the SSR CTCM element moves to element 5). On this line, 4 is the element number, TK OK shows the ticketing arrangement, 25SEP is the creation date, and XXXXXXXXX after the slash is the hidden office ID. In Amadeus, whether TK is mandatory before saving a booking depends on the office's settings, and in DEIXEN's practice office it is mandatory: if TK is missing when you try to end the transaction, the system returns the error message NEED TICKETING ARRANGEMENT. Next, you will add the final mandatory PRINT element, RF.
L07-RF.title: Record who asked for the booking: RF
L07-RF.objective: Add the Received From element with RF naming the person who requested the booking, and recognize how DEIXEN confirms it before filing.
L07-RF.body:
Before saving a PNR or any changes to it, the reservation agent must record who requested the booking or instructed the change. This is the Received From element — the R in PRINT — added with the command RF. A PNR cannot be filed with ER unless a Received From element has been entered.

Build the entry in two parts: the fixed command code RF, followed immediately by free text naming the person who requested the booking. For example, in the official Amadeus example where Mr Smith requested the booking, the entry is RFMR SMITH (or RFGEORGE for a caller named George, and in DEIXEN's demonstration booking for Mr Omar Salem, RFMR SALEM). In your DEIXEN task, read the task brief to see who requested the booking (the passenger himself) and write RF followed by his name or title and surname.

Because official Amadeus documentation does not show how the screen displays RF before the transaction ends, DEIXEN confirms your entry with a training message — for example, Received From recorded: MR SALEM. — and shows an unnumbered training row at the bottom of the booking panel until you file the booking. Once you end the transaction with ER in the next step, the RF element no longer appears in the active booking display because Amadeus moves it into the booking's history.
L08-ER.title: End the transaction with ER
L08-ER.objective: Verify that all mandatory booking elements are present, end the transaction with ER to file the PNR, and read the six-character record locator in the completed booking header.
L08-ER.body:
Up to this point, the reservation agent has built the PNR in a temporary working session. To file (save) the booking in the system, the agent must end the transaction. Before typing the command, check that your booking has all five mandatory PRINT elements — Phone, Received from (RF), Itinerary (SS), Name (NM), and Ticketing (TK) — plus the passenger contact SSR for the airline (SRCTCM or SRCTCR). In this DEIXEN training task, the agency phone number is added using AP. Amadeus provides two commands to end a transaction: ER ends the transaction and immediately redisplays the saved PNR on screen, whereas ET ends the transaction without redisplaying it. Because you will price the booking on screen in step 9, type the two-letter entry ER.

If a required element is missing when you enter ER, the booking is not filed cleanly. If the ticketing arrangement (TK) is missing, Amadeus returns the error message NEED TICKETING ARRANGEMENT; recover by entering TKOK and then typing ER again (as shown in DEIXEN's demonstration for this lesson). If the booking has no passenger contact SSR (none of SRCTCM, SRCTCE, or SRCTCR), Amadeus returns the warning MISSING SSR CTCM MOBILE OR SSR CTCE EMAIL OR SSR CTCR NON-CONSENT. In Amadeus, typing ER a second time bypasses that warning and files the booking, but the system records the bypass in the PNR's history. In DEIXEN's tasks and scenario, never bypass the warning with a second ER: recover by adding the required contact SSR (SRCTCM with the passenger's mobile, or SRCTCR-REFUSED if the passenger declined) and then enter ER.

When ER succeeds, the system files the PNR and returns the completed booking display. In DEIXEN's demonstration booking, the header line now expands to: RP/XXXXXXXXX/XXXXXXXXX            XX/XX 25SEP26/1200Z   K7P2M9, followed by the five numbered elements (1.SALEM/OMAR MR, 2 6X 101 M 15OCT 4 RUHJED HK1 ..., 3 AP 966120000000, 4 TK OK25SEP/XXXXXXXXX, and 5 SSR CTCM 6X HK1 966500000009). On the expanded header line, read from left to right: RP/ (header start), the responsible and queueing office IDs (XXXXXXXXX/XXXXXXXXX), the agent sign and duty code (XX/XX), the filing date and time in Z (UTC) format (25SEP26/1200Z), and at the far right the six-character record locator (such as K7P2M9, or 24526Z in the official Amadeus example). The record locator is the unique six-character reference code used to retrieve the saved PNR in the system. Notice also that the RF line has moved into the booking's history and no longer appears in the list. Your PNR is now filed and ready to price with FXP.
L09-FXP.title: Price the booking with FXP
L09-FXP.objective: Price the filed PNR in its booked class and store the pricing record with FXP, and read the passenger, flight, fare basis, and total lines on the pricing display.
L09-FXP.body:
Once the PNR is filed, the reservation agent calculates the fare and taxes for the passenger's itinerary. In Amadeus, pricing the booking in the booking class already reserved and saving that calculation in the PNR creates a Transitional Stored Ticket (TST): a stored pricing record attached to the booking. Amadeus has two related pricing commands: FXP prices the itinerary in the booked class and stores a TST, whereas FXX calculates and displays the price without storing a TST (FXX is not simulated in this DEIXEN slice). To price the booking and store the TST, type the three-letter entry FXP.

Because only one fare applies in this DEIXEN slice, entering FXP returns the single-fare pricing display directly. In DEIXEN's demonstration booking (for 1 seat on 6X 101 in booking class M from RUH to JED), the pricing display starts with the passenger header 01 SALEM/OMAR* and the last date to ticket line LAST TKT DTE 15OCT26 - SEE ADV PURCHASE, followed by the flight table: RUH 6X 101 M 15OCT 0700 OK M1OW                 15OCT15OCT 1P and JED, and then the fare and tax summary ending with SAR    450.00 (base fare), SAR     80.00YR (tax), and TOTAL   SAR    530.00. Read the key parts of this display from top to bottom: 01 SALEM/OMAR* names the passenger being priced; in the flight row, RUH and JED are the origin and destination, 6X 101 is the airline and flight number, M is the booking class, 15OCT and 0700 are the departure date and time, OK is the status, M1OW is the fare basis (the code that identifies the specific fare and its rules), 15OCT15OCT are the validity dates, and 1P is the baggage allowance (one piece). Below the flight table, the currency and amounts show the base fare (SAR 450.00), the tax amount and code (SAR 80.00YR), and the total price to collect (TOTAL SAR 530.00). Completing FXP finishes the nine required steps of the booking and pricing path in this DEIXEN slice.

In live Amadeus operations, if several fares apply to the booked class, FXP displays a numbered list of fares first, and the reservation agent selects the chosen fare with the command FXT followed by the fare line number (for example, FXT02, or FXT2/P1,2 for multiple passengers). Because only one fare applies in DEIXEN's practice routes, you never need FXT in this slice.
L10-FQD.title: Optional: look at fares with FQD
L10-FQD.objective: Display published fares for a city pair using the optional command FQD, and read the fare lines in the fare display.
L10-FQD.body:
Before or outside a specific booking, a reservation agent may want to look up the fares offered between two cities. The command FQD requests a fare display: a table of fares for a city pair, independent of any PNR (unlike FXP, which prices a filed PNR). In DEIXEN, this tenth lesson is optional and is not required to complete the nine-step booking and pricing path, assessment, or scenario.

Build the basic entry in two parts with no spaces: the fixed command code FQD, followed immediately by the six-letter city pair (the origin code and the destination code written together). For example, in the official Amadeus example for Amsterdam (AMS) to New York (NYC), the entry is FQDAMSNYC; in DEIXEN's demonstration route for Riyadh (RUH) to Jeddah (JED), the entry is FQDRUHJED.

When you enter FQDRUHJED in DEIXEN's demonstration, the fare display shows a header line ROE 3.750000 NEAREST 1.00 SAR, a date and route line 25SEP26**25SEP26/RUHJED, a column header line LN FARE BASIS OW   SAR  RT   B PEN  DATES/DAYS   AP MIN MAX R, and numbered fare rows such as 01 M1OW          450.00      M  -       -     -   -  -   -  6X and 02 Y1OW          650.00      Y  -       -     -   -  -   -  6X, ending with PAGE 1/1. Read each fare row from left to right: LN is the two-digit line number (01, 02), FARE BASIS is the fare basis code (M1OW, Y1OW), OW SAR is the one-way fare amount in the display currency (450.00, 650.00), and B is the single-letter booking class for that fare (M, Y); the airline code (6X) appears at the right end of the row (columns shown with a dash - are not used in this practice display).

In live Amadeus operations, optional modifiers can be added after the city pair, each preceded by a slash (/), and a + or @ symbol next to a fare indicates that fare rules can be read with the command FQN followed by the line number. Modifiers on FQD and the command FQN are outside this DEIXEN slice.
task.title: Book and price a one-way flight
task.brief: Mr Saad Alharbi wants one seat from Riyadh (RUH) to Dubai (DXB) on {TASK_DATE}, on flight 6X 403 in class Y. Your agency's phone: 966110000000. His mobile for the airline: 966500000001. Ticketing arrangement: TKOK. He requested the booking himself. Build the booking, end the transaction, then price it.
scn.title: Scenario: the passenger refuses to give a mobile number
scn.brief: Mr Fahad Alqahtani wants one seat from Jeddah (JED) to Dubai (DXB) on {SCN_DATE}, on flight 6X 515 in class B. Your agency's phone: 966110000000. When you ask for his mobile number or e-mail for the airline, he says he does not want to share them. Ticketing arrangement: TKOK. He requested the booking himself. Build the booking, end the transaction, then price it.
scn.objective: Complete and price the booking while recording, correctly, that the passenger refused to share contact details with the airline.
scn.constraints: One adult, one flight, class B on 6X 515. No mobile number or e-mail is available. Do not invent contact details and do not bypass the end-of-transaction warning.
an.fb.format: This entry doesn't follow the availability pattern. Compare its parts, in order, with the pattern in the lesson.
an.fb.dateRange: The date is outside the period an availability display covers.
an.fb.taskMismatch: The entry is valid, but the date or the city pair is not the one in the task.
ss.fb.noDisplay: There is no availability display to sell from yet.
ss.fb.format: This entry doesn't follow the short-sell pattern. Check each part and its order.
ss.fb.lineMissing: The line number in your entry isn't in the last availability display.
ss.fb.seats: The number of seats doesn't match the number of passengers in the task.
ss.fb.class: The class in your entry isn't the class the task asks for — or the line isn't the task's flight.
nm.fb.format: This name entry doesn't follow the name pattern. Check the separator between surname and first name, and the title.
nm.fb.count: The passenger count in the name entry doesn't match the task.
nm.fb.name: The name doesn't match the passenger in the task. Check the spelling.
ap.fb.format: The contact element has no text after AP.
ap.fb.phone: The contact element doesn't contain the phone number the task gives.
ctc.fb.format: This contact SSR doesn't follow the pattern. Compare it, part by part, with the pattern in the lesson.
ctc.fb.number: The number in the contact SSR isn't the passenger's mobile from the task.
ctc.fb.refusalNotTask: This passenger gave a mobile number for the airline. A recorded refusal would not match what the passenger told you.
scn.fb.ctcmInvented: This passenger did not give a mobile number. A contact SSR with a number would not match what the passenger told you.
scn.fb.warningShown: The warning lists three ways to satisfy it. Which one matches this passenger's answer?
scn.fb.bypassed: The booking was filed without recording the passenger's refusal. The bypass is recorded in the booking's history, and this step does not count as correct.
tk.fb.format: This isn't one of the two ticketing arrangement entries.
tk.fb.variant: The ticketing arrangement is valid, but it isn't the one the task asks for.
rf.fb.format: RF needs free text naming who requested the booking.
er.fb.missing: The booking isn't complete yet: at least one required element is missing.
er.fb.bypassed: The booking was filed without a passenger contact SSR. The bypass is recorded in the booking's history, and this step does not count as correct.
fxp.fb.format: This isn't the pricing entry used in this step.
fxp.fb.noPnr: There is no complete booking to price yet.
fqd.fb.format: This entry doesn't follow the fare display pattern.
fqd.fb.route: The city pair isn't the task's route.
er.partial.name: Missing: the passenger name.
er.partial.contactSsr: Missing: the passenger contact SSR for the airline.
reveal.AN: Type {EXPECTED_ENTRY} — AN, the date, then the city pair.
reveal.SS: Type {EXPECTED_ENTRY} — seats, class, then the line number of the task's flight.
reveal.CTC: Type {EXPECTED_ENTRY} — the dash after SRCTCM is mandatory.
reveal.ER: Add the missing element first, then type ER. Missing now: {MISSING_LIST}
nudge.FORMAT: Look at the shape of your entry: a part is missing, extra, or out of order.
nudge.DATA_REFERENCE: The entry's shape is fine; one value in it doesn't match what it refers to.
nudge.AVAILABILITY: What you asked for isn't available in the display.
nudge.GENERAL: Something in this entry isn't accepted. Re-read the task step.
nudge.SEQUENCE: This entry needs something that has to come before it.
nudge.MANDATORY_MISSING: A required element of the booking is still missing.
nudge.DUPLICATE_CONFLICT: This conflicts with something already in the booking.
nudge.LOGICAL: The entry is valid, but it doesn't match the task.
tm.notForTask: Entry not used: it does not match the task.
tm.notCovered: This entry is not covered in this slice of DEIXEN. It may be a real Amadeus entry; DEIXEN does not simulate it yet.
tm.noPracticeData: DEIXEN has practice flights only for the task's route in this slice.
tm.classNotOffered: In this practice display that class shows 0. The real Amadeus response to selling such a class is not verified, so DEIXEN does not simulate it.
tm.fxpBeforeName: In this slice, pricing is practiced on a booking that already has a name and a flight.
tm.rfMissing: The booking was not filed: the Received From element is missing. (The exact Amadeus wording of this message is not verified.)
tm.otherMissing: DEIXEN did not file the booking: an element this task requires is missing. (How Amadeus responds here is not verified.)
tm.secondName: This slice practices one adult passenger only.
tm.rfLine: Received From recorded: {RF_TEXT}. (How Amadeus displays RF before the end of the transaction is not verified.)
tm.ctcrLine: Contact refusal recorded (SRCTCR): {CTCR_TEXT}. (How Amadeus displays it is not verified.)
tm.sliceEnd: The slice ends at the pricing display. What happens to the stored pricing record afterwards is not simulated.
coach.needTk: This is a real Amadeus message. It means a required element is missing: the ticketing arrangement.
coach.missingCtc: This is a real Amadeus warning. The booking has no contact SSR for the airline: a mobile number, an e-mail, or a recorded refusal.
coach.bypassRecorded: Entering ER again bypasses the warning, and the bypass is recorded in the booking's history.
coach.erDone: The transaction is ended. The last part of the header line is the record locator.
coach.fxpDone: The booking is priced and the result is stored as a TST.
coach.escalate: Errors of this kind on this step in this session: {N}. Do you want to open the lesson again?
coach.growth.reinforce: Needs practice again: {COMMANDS}. A new error came after earlier correct entries.
coach.growth.assessmentUnmet: The last assessment did not count every step as correct. A new assessment can show the full path working.
ui.unverifiedMarker: Official Amadeus pattern; small details may differ in the real system, so don't memorise them.
ui.dash.notOwn: Correct, not yet on your own
ui.dash.notCompleted: Not yet completed with every step correct
ui.assessment.intro: You are starting the assessment: the full booking and pricing path. The result comes only from the entries you make in this assessment: the path counts as working when you end the transaction with ER and then price the booking with FXP, both correct. Hints stay available; each one you use is counted and shown with the result. Earlier sessions are not included.

disc.title: What this simulator does and does not do
disc.1: DEIXEN is a practice simulator, not Amadeus. All flights, seats, fares, taxes, names, phone numbers, office codes and record locators are invented for practice. The airline code 6X is used only as a practice code; no real schedule or fare is shown.
disc.2: Only these entries are simulated: AN, SS, NM, AP, SRCTCM, SRCTCR, TK, RF, ER, FXP, and FQD (optional). Another entry that DEIXEN's Amadeus reference names as a real Amadeus entry (for example FXX or FQN) gets the message 'not covered in this slice' — a DEIXEN limit, not an Amadeus one. Any other entry gets the training message 'Entry not recognized.': DEIXEN does not recognize it, which does not mean that Amadeus would reject it.
disc.3: This slice practices one adult passenger, one flight, and one applicable fare. Real Amadeus also handles children and infants, several passengers and flights, groups, and fare lists where you choose a fare with FXT.
disc.4: DEIXEN's practice office requires a ticketing arrangement (TK) before the transaction can end. In real Amadeus this depends on the office's settings.
disc.5: Lines marked 'Training message' are DEIXEN's own words. The real Amadeus wording of many error messages is not publicly documented, so DEIXEN does not imitate it.
disc.6: Screens follow the layout of official Amadeus examples. Column spacing may differ. Some details appear in official examples only in part, or without their meaning: the codes in the availability display (the number before the weekday, the figure after each class letter, the E0 code), the header time when you enter a time, the airline code and HK1 in a stored mobile-contact line, and the booking display after AP, SRCTCM, SRCTCR, TK and RF entries. DEIXEN marks these displays with a dashed line and the note 'Official Amadeus pattern; small details may differ in the real system, so don't memorise them.' The one-letter codes after the equipment in a flight line before the transaction ends also appear in official examples without their meaning. DEIXEN does not teach any of these details: when you show a display's names, each of them has a dashed line and 'not taught'. Where no official example exists at all (a stored SRCTCR line; RF before the transaction ends), DEIXEN shows a training message instead. DEIXEN does not show the tags above the header line (such as RLR or TST) or airline messages under a sold flight. The fare display (FQD) shows no notice lines, and its date line leaves out the global indicator and the mileage figures.
disc.7: Practice flights exist only for the task routes. The meaning of some codes on the screens (for example the figures after class letters) is not taught, because DEIXEN could not verify it from official sources. Official examples of SRCTCM and SRCTCR end with an extra part (for example /US or /P3); what that part must contain is not covered in this slice, and DEIXEN accepts the entry with or without it.
disc.8: The slice ends at the pricing display. It does not simulate what happens to the stored pricing record afterwards, or ticket issuance.
disc.9: 'Correct in DEIXEN' means your entry met this simulator's checklist. 'Done on your own' on the booking chain means you have made at least one correct entry for that step with no help for that entry: no hint, no demonstration and no feedback that gave away the answer. Neither is a certificate of workplace readiness.

ghost.ann.L01.1: The header line names the display, the destination, the weekday, the date and a time.
ghost.ann.L01.2: Each flight line starts with its line number — the next step, SS, uses it — then the airline code and the flight number.
ghost.ann.L01.3: Then the booking classes, one letter for each class.
ghost.ann.L01.4: Then the origin and the destination, the departure and arrival times, and the flying time.
ghost.ann.L01.5: Then the equipment code. The parts with a dashed line are not taught: DEIXEN could not verify what they mean.
ghost.ann.L02.1: Amadeus answers with the booking as it now stands, under its header line.
ghost.ann.L02.2: The flight sold is element 1 of the booking: the airline code, the flight number and the booking class.
ghost.ann.L02.3: Then the date, the day of the week as a number, and the origin and destination written together.
ghost.ann.L02.4: HK1 is the status with the seat count. Then the departure and arrival times and the equipment code.
ghost.ann.L02.5: The codes with a dashed line are not taught.
ghost.ann.L08.1: After ER, the header line has more parts: the office IDs, the agent sign and duty code, the date and time, and the record locator used to retrieve the booking.
ghost.ann.L08.2: The last element is the passenger contact SSR, with the mobile number for the airline. The parts with a dashed line are not taught.
